lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Shall we settle the accounts, ferryman? See what you owe me already, so we don't end up arguing about it again.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Let's do it, Hermes. Better to have it sorted and no trouble later.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: I brought you that anchor you ordered — five drachmas.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: By Hades, that's what I paid for it, and the rope was two obols.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Five drachmas and two obols, then.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And the needle for the sail — I laid out five obols for that.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Wax to patch the leaks in the boat, nails, and the cord you made the halyard from — two drachmas for the lot.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: That's everything, unless something else slipped our minds in the reckoning. So when do you plan to pay this back?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Can't do it now, Hermes. But if a plague or a war sends a crowd down all at once, then I can make it up by shorting the fares.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: So now I'm supposed to sit here praying for the worst, just to get paid?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: No other way. Right now, as you see, only a few are coming our way. It's peacetime.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Better that way, even if you keep stretching out the debt. Still, the old ones, Charon — you know how they arrived: all brave, most of them bloody and wounded. Now it's either someone poisoned by his son or his wife, or bloated from luxury, pale and low-born, nothing like those. And most of them come over money, scheming against each other, by the look of it.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Those things are very desirable, after all.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: So I wouldn't seem wrong to demand the money you owe me rather sharply.
